newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar, gold slip, Euro shares mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar, gold slip, Euro shares mixed.

text.p: The dollar began European trading lower on Monday, hit by data showing a rising Japanese trade surplus, while gold, languishing at 12-year lows, slipped another $6 an ounce.
Key European stock markets lacked a fresh lead from Wall Street, which was closed for a holiday on Friday, and were mixed after hitting records during the previous week.
The yen was boosted to four-week highs against the dollar in earlier Asian trading after news of a 129.3 percent year-on-year gain in Japan's trade surplus for the first 20 days of June.
"The rising Japan surplus is likely to keep the yen strong for now but this data is still a reflection of the weak yen from the first half of the year," said a U.S. bank dealer.
The dollar also came under pressure as the pound lost almost two pfennigs due to data showing a sharp drop in British industrial output -- which analysts said was mainly due to sterling's strength.
The U.S. currency suffered further from fallout from market nerves over Europe's unsteady progress towards economic and monetary union (EMU).
As some senior German politicians continue to speak out for a delay in EMU rather than softening qualification criteria, the mark has gained favour.

In an interview in the Financial Times, Bavarian prime minister Edmund Stoiber, a member of the Christian Social Union party of Theo Waigel, Germany's finance minister, said a delay in EMU would be preferable to a weak single currency.
"A controlled delay would certainly be better than a weak European currency," Stoiber was quoted as saying. "It would mean holding to the goal of the euro and holding firm to the criteria."
Gold plunged to 12-year lows last week after confirmation that the Reserve Bank of Australia had sold 167 tonnes from its gold reserves raised bullion market fears of sales by other central banks.
It had dropped a further $6 from Friday's late levels in early London business and traders said it could continue to decline.
In equity trading, the London stock market reversed to show a loss of around half a percent after earlier gains, while Paris was a third of a percent lower and Frankfurt the same amount higher.

The London market, Europe's biggest, was dragged down by a fall in futures as speculation on a rise in interest rates this week took hold and outweighed the impact of more takeover bid talk concerning banks.
"In theory the market should be subject to a bit of profit-taking because of the strength of sterling and the possibility of an interest rate rise this week," said one senior dealer.
Britain's latest building society-turned-bank to float on the stock market, Woolwich WWH.L, topped its tipped debut level of around 320 pence at 362 after a high of 370.

Elsewhere, key areas of interest for markets will be a meeting of European Union finance ministers to discuss Italy's plans for qualifying for the single currency and comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer's after a monthly meeting of Group of 10 central bankers in Basle.
CURRENCIES AT 0915 GMT
The dollar was around 112.35 yen and 1.7437 marks, compared with 113.74 and 1.7565 in late European business on Friday.
Sterling was around 2.9340 marks versus 2.9597 late on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0915 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 26.3 points or 0.55 percent at 4,786.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was 9.25 points or 0.32 percent lower at 2,925.23.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 12.23 points or 0.31 percent at 3,954.76.
PRECIOUS METALS
London gold slid to around $318.75 an ounce from Friday's late London level of $324.50. Silver declined six cents to $4.49.
